question: In preparation of NaOH by electrolytic method, which solution is used?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brine**__**.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Sodium hydroxide

 
 
• **Sodium hydroxide** is industrially produced as a **50 percent** solution by variations of the electrolytic chloralkali process. Chlorine gas is also produced in this process. Solid sodium hydroxide is obtained from this solution by the evaporation of water.
 
• Various methods of preparation of sodium hydroxide are -
 
 
 
• **Castner-Kellner Process**
 
 
• In the** Castner-Kellner method,** **NaOH** is prepared by the electrolysis of an aqueous solution of **NaCl (Brine).**
 
• **Castner-Kellner cell**- lt is a **rectangular tank of steel**. Inside of the tank is lined with 'ebonite.' The anode is made of titanium. A flowing layer of mercury Hg at the bottom of the tank serves as the cathode.
 
• When an **electric current** is passed through the brine, **+ve** and **-ve **ions migrate toward their respective electrodes. **Na+** ions are discharged at the **mercury** cathode.
 
• The **sodium** deposited in mercury forms **Sodium Amalgam**. The chlorine produced at the anode is removed from the top of the cell. reaction at cathode** Na+** ions are discharged in preference to** H+** ions due to **high overvoltage**.
